idea.body: A rigid transformation moves every point of a figure by the same rule, without changing any length or angle. A translation slides a point by a fixed amount: (x, y) becomes (x + a, y + b). A reflection flips a point over a line: over the x-axis it becomes (x, -y), and over the y-axis it becomes (-x, y). A rotation about the origin turns a point through an angle. 90 degrees counterclockwise sends (x, y) to (-y, x); 180 degrees sends it to (-x, -y). For example, reflecting the point (3, 5) over the x-axis gives (3, -5): the x-coordinate stays put and the y-coordinate changes sign. Each rule is worth memorizing, since every problem is just substitution once you know which rule applies.

figure.alt: The point (3, 5) and its reflection (3, -5) over the x-axis.

workedExample.prompt: Point A is at (2, 5). Reflect A over the line y = x, then translate the result 2 units right and 6 units down. What is the final image?
steps: Reflecting over y = x swaps the coordinates: (2, 5) becomes (5, 2).
Translating 2 units right adds 2 to the x-coordinate: 5 + 2 = 7.
Translating 6 units down subtracts 6 from the y-coordinate: 2 - 6 = -4.

figure.alt: Point (2, 5), its reflection (5, 2) over y = x, and the final image (7, -4).

ways.name: The rule on coordinates
ways.when: Use this any time you know which transformation applies and need one image point.
steps: Reflecting over the x-axis keeps x the same and flips the sign of y.
Each transformation has its own rule: substitute the coordinates directly into it.
ways.example: Reflect the point (3, 5) over the x-axis.
ways.trap: Flipping the sign of x instead of y when reflecting over the x-axis.

figure.alt: The point (3, 5) and its reflection (3, -5) over the x-axis.

ways.name: Trace and slide, flip or turn
ways.when: Use this when picturing the motion helps more than computing coordinates.
steps: Trace the figure on paper, then physically slide, flip or turn the tracing.
A slide moves the tracing without turning it.
A flip turns the tracing face down over a line.
A turn rotates the tracing around one fixed point.
Read the new coordinates straight off the moved tracing.
ways.example: Picture point (2, 3) flipped over a mirror line by turning a tracing over.
ways.trap: Sliding the tracing sideways instead of flipping it over the line.

figure.alt: A point beside a mirror line, then flipped across it to the other side.

frames.caption: Start: point (2, 3) beside the mirror line.
Flip it straight across the line.

ways.name: The vector for a translation
ways.when: Use this when a translation is described as a shift, not separate coordinate rules.
steps: A translation vector of (5, -3) means move 5 right and 3 down.
ways.example: Translate the point (1, 4) by the vector (5, -3).
ways.trap: Adding the vector's second number instead of subtracting when it is negative.

figure.alt: The point (1, 4) shifted by the vector (5, -3) to (6, 1).

ways.name: The composition one step at a time
ways.when: Use this when two or more transformations happen one after another.
steps: Reflect over y = x first: swap the coordinates to get (1, 3).
Translate that result 4 right and 2 up: (1 + 4, 3 + 2).
That is (5, 5), the final image after both steps.
ways.example: Reflect (3, 1) over y = x, then translate 4 right and 2 up.
ways.trap: Doing the two transformations in the wrong order, which can change the final point.

figure.alt: Point B(3, 1) reflected to (1, 3), then translated to (5, 5).
